newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE to launch options market in October.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE to launch options market in October.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange announced on Monday it planned to launch an equity options market in October 1997.

In a statement, the exchange said the options market -- to be known as the EOM, would list standardised American style scrip-settled call and put options on the equities underlying the ALSI40, GLDI10, INDI25 and the FINDI30 indices.
"This policy will provide traded options on approximately 50 blue chip stocks, representing a broad spectrum of investment and hedging opportunities in major companies listed on the JSE," it said.
The options expiry cycle would conform with the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) futures expiry to facilitate arbitrage between Safex contracts and the EOM contracts.
The listing of index options would be considered when appropriate, the exchange said.
Trading would initially be conducted on a "screen and telephone" basis before moving to an automated system at a later date.

A separate clearing house would be established to provide the register of all option contracts and administer all market positions, while exercised options would be settled through the existing JSE equity market clearing house.
The exchange said it would invite applications for membership of the EOM through the acquisition of seats, which are to be issued at a price of 85,000 rand each.
Applications for membership close on March 14 and the exchange said it would announced results of the issue of seats and membership on March 27.
